answer: Each identity may claim only one horizon delta gauge: it installs the gauge at one delta reach, pays a deployment fee, and files a key-signed reading at the haven horizon tide. An auditor replays the gauge serial, reach, and timestamp against the tide log; a reused serial, duplicated reach, or reading over 5% from the logged delta voids the claim and bars the key. The kth gauge costs 31+8(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 8023 and 1,000 fakes cost 4,027,000 in fees. A rented-gauge ring fails because one serial cannot cover two reaches at the same haven moment. An honest agent pays 31.
